'''Alain Brillet''' ({{IPA|fr|alɛ̃ bʁijɛ}}; 30 March 1947 – 20 March 2026) was a French physicist who specialised in [[Gravitational-wave observatory|gravitational wave detectors]].

== Life and career ==
Alain Brillet was born on 30 March 1947. He graduated from the [[ESPCI Paris]] in 1970, following which he worked for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] in [[Orsay]] during his Ph.D. thesis until 1976. He later worked in [[Boulder, Colorado|Boulder]] with [[John L. Hall|John Hall]], before returning to France in 1982. He was most famous for being one of the two fathers of the [[Virgo interferometer]] with [[Adalberto Giazotto]], directing the consortium during its design and construction between 1989 and 2003.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Etienne |first=Véronique |date=27 September 2017 |title=Alain Brillet et Thibault Damour, physiciens, lauréats 2017 d'une double médaille d'or du CNRS {{!}} CNRS |url=https://www.cnrs.fr/fr/alain-brillet-et-thibault-damour-physiciens-laureats-2017-dune-double-medaille-dor-du-cnrs |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=www.cnrs.fr |language=fr}}</ref>

He was awarded the [[Ampère Prize]] in 2016<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lauréat 2016 du prix Ampère de l’Électricité de France : Alain Brillet {{!}} Lauréats {{!}} Prix et médailles {{!}} Encourager la vie scientifique |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Laureats/laureat-2016-du-prix-ampere-de-l-electricite-de-france-alain-brillet.html |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=www.academie-sciences.fr}}</ref> and the [[CNRS Gold Medal]] in 2017<ref name=":0" /> for his work on the Virgo detector.

Brillet died on 20 March 2026, at the age of 78.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ansa.it/canale_scienza/notizie/biotech/2026/03/20/addio-ad-alain-brillet-fra-i-pionieri-della-ricerca-sulle-onde-gravitazionali_49c926e1-6cb7-428e-b059-eab9d0ce6126.html|title=Addio ad Alain Brillet, fra i pionieri della ricerca sulle onde gravitazionali|language=it|date=20 March 2026|access-date=20 March 2026}}</ref>
